FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Public Health Engineering Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineering Divisional 
Council. 


Underdrainage systems in a rapid sand gravity filter perform two main functions: 
a) Collecting filtered water uniformly throughout the filter bed area and carrying it to outlet chambers. 


b) Distributing compressed air, where provided and wash water during washing operation in such a fashion 
that entire portion of the bed perform the same amount of work. 


Since the rate of wash water is many times higher than that of filtration, the design of under drains is governed by 
up-flow requirements. 


IS 8419 (Part 1) : 1977 ‘Requirements for filtration equipment: Part 1 Filtration media — Sand and gravel’ was 
formulated to cover requirements for sand and gravel for use as filtration medium for treatment of water. 
Subsequently, IS 8419 (Part 2) : 1984 “Requirements for rapid sand gravity filtration equipment: Part 2 
Underdrainage system” was formulated to cover requirements for underdrainage system for rapid sand gravity 
filtration equipment. Considering that IS 8419 (Part 1) did not specifically cover requirements of sand and gravel 
filtration medium for rapid sand gravity filters, the technical committee responsible for the formulation of this 
standard decided to prepare a new standard for covering requirements of filter sand and gravel as presently 
covered in IS 8419 (Part 1). Accordingly, the specification for sand and gravel for use as filtration medium has 
been covered in IS 17955 : 2023 “Sand and gravel for use as filtration medium — Specification”. IS 8419 (Part 2) 
has been revised as IS 8419 : 2023 ‘Underdrainage system of rapid sand gravity filtration equipment —— 
Requirements (first revision)”. Further, in this revision of the standard, experience gained over the years in the 
use of standard has been utilized. The following major modifications have been incorporated in this revision of 
the standard: 


a) Use of cast iron pipes in manifolds and laterals of pipe grid systems has been deleted; 

b) Use of ductile iron pipes and glass reinforced plastic pipes for manifolds and laterals in pipe grid systems 
has been included; 

c) Use of glazed stoneware pipes for laterals in pipe grid with nozzle underdrainage system has been 
deleted; 

d) Reference to concerned Indian standards for unplasticized polyvinyl chloride (UPVC) and polyethylene 
tees (fittings) have been mentioned; 

e) Use of stainless strips in place of asbestos strips in pipe grid with nozzle underdrainage system has been 
specified; and 

f) Grade designations of grey iron casting for use in saddle and stainless steel for use in clamp and hook 
belt have been aligned as per the latest product/standards specification. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex B. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 2022 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)’. The number of significant places 
retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 8419 : 2023 


Indian Standard 


UNDERDRAINAGE SYSTEM OF RAPID SAND GRAVITY 
FILTRATION EQUIPMENT — REQUIREMENTS 


( First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard lays down the requirements of pipe 
grid types and false bottom floor types 
underdrainage system of rapid sand gravity filtration 
equipment for water treatment plants. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed in Annex A contain provisions, 
which through reference in this text, constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of 
publication, the editions indicated were valid. All 
standards are subject to revision and parties to 
agreement based on these standards are encouraged 
to investigate the possibility of applying the most 
recent editions of these standards. 


3 PIPE GRID TYPES 


Following are the two types of underdrainage 
system: 


a) Pipe grid without nozzles; and 
b) Pipe grid with nozzles. 


3.1 Pipe Grid without Nozzles 


3.1.1 This comprises a main called manifold or 
header and perforated laterals. 


3.1.2 Material of Construction 


Material of construction for pipe grid without 
nozzles underdrainage system is given in Table 1. 


3.1.3 Construction 


3.1.3.1 The manifold is in the form of pipe or 
reinforced cement concrete (RCC) duct below the 
floor of filter. Top of this duct should be covered by 
in-situ ВСС slab of minimum grade М 20 leaving 
one or two convenient gaps to remove shuttering. 
These gaps should be covered with precast slabs. 
The size of precast slab should not exceed 0.6 m? in 
area. Reinforcement of precast slabs are jointed with 
reinforcement of floor and concrete is poured for 
floor, covering precast slab joints also. 


NOTE — No reinforcement should be left exposed since 
these are likely to be corroded. 


3.1.3.2 Perforations should be drilled into the 
laterals in a single row of orifices directed 
vertically downward or in two rows as pair of 
orifices directed downward at a suitable angle on 
either side of the vertical diameter and spacing of 
orifices/perforations will be governed by the 
hydraulic design. 


3.2 Pipe Grid with Nozzles 


3.2.1 This comprises a main called manifold or 
header and laterals with nozzles. 


3.2.2 Material of Construction 


Material of construction of pipe grid with 
nozzles underdrainage system is given in 
Table 2. 


3.2.3 Construction 


3.2.3.1 The filter floor should consist of a series 
of lateral pipes each connecting to a central 
channel or manifold and fitted with nozzles. The 
pipes should have holes on the top to receive 
bosses, or ‘nozzle plates’ in which the nozzles 
are screwed. The portions of the pipes bridging 
the channel, formed in the floor of the filter tank 
should have slots on the undersides. All the pipes 
should be grouted to the floor and embedded in 
concrete with suitable reinforcement, after which 
the hole should be screeded to a smooth surface 
flush with the upper faces of the nozzle plates. 
The nozzles should then be screwed into the 
position. 


3.2.3.2 The compressed air for the air scour, 
where provided should be brought through 
header pipes, located at angles to the floor 
laterals. The headers are tapped and fitted with 
small bore tubes connecting into the laterals 
through additional bosses similar to those for the 
nozzles. 


3.2.3.3 The pipe for the filtered water outlet and up 
wash inlet should be connected into the manifold at 
the front end of the filter. 


IS 8419 : 2023

4 FALSE BOTTOM FLOOR TYPE 


4.1 Filter floors which replace pipe side, serve two 
functions: 


a) Support the filter bed; and 

b) Create a waterway beneath the filter for 
collecting filtered water and for distributing 
the wash water. 


4.2 The floor, depending upon its thickness, should 
be perforated by short tubes or orifices of such 
dimension as to introduce the controlling loss of 
head and provide an even distribution of wash water. 
The openings should be relatively small and closely 
spaced. 


4.3 Construction 


4.3.1 This should consist of either precast slab or 
cast-in-situ slabs to which the nozzles are fitted. An 
internal threaded bush should be grouted in concrete 
and nozzles screwed into it. Nozzles should be 
made of UPVC/PE/stainless steel/brass. 


IS 1570 (Part 5) 


4.3.2 Precast slabs should rest on either ВСС stub 
columns or series of beams or dwarf walls. For 
holding the precast slabs against uplift during back 
washing, bolts, nuts and washers of stainless steel 
should be used. To provide uniform bearing pressure 
on the underside of precast slabs, stainless steel or 
brass strips should be used on the edges resting on 
beams or dwarf walls. Precast slab edges are filled 
with bituminous compound for sealing, for which 
edges should be provided with grooves. 


4.3.3 For cast in-situ slab, nozzle bushes should be 
held in suitable fixtures while concreting for 
uniform pitching and leveling of bushes. 


4.3.4 For uniform distribution along the length of 
filter, a header channel, normally below the waste 
water gullet inside the filter should be provided. This 
header channel is provided with necessary openings 
at top and bottom on two side vertical walls for 
uniform distribution of back wash water and air.

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Head (Publication & Sales), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in.
